OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized by
            removing every non-digit character and must contain exactly 10 digits
            afterwards; the normalized 10-digit value is stored and returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be a
            syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. When
            omitted on create it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true on create, allows the owner to be created even if another owner
            already has the same last name and address (i.e. they knowingly share a
            household). When false or omitted, such a create is rejected with 409 Conflict.
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true

## Summary

I consolidated the three separate duplicate checks (telephone, email, household) into a single derived `identityKey` and rejected creates only on a whole-key match.

**Changes:**

1. **`OwnerRestControllerV1`** (`rest/controller/v1/`):
   - Added `deriveIdentityKey(telephone, email, householdId)` → `normalizedTelephone + "|" + (email or "") + "|" + (householdId or "")`.
   - Replaced `rejectDuplicateTelephone`/`rejectDuplicateEmail`/`rejectDuplicateHousehold` with a single `rejectDuplicateIdentity(key)` that throws only when the new owner's whole key equals an existing owner's (each existing owner's key derived from its stored normalized telephone/email/householdId).
   - Removed the three separate check calls and their now-unused imports.

2. **`householdId` semantics** — this was the crux. A literal reading (`householdId` always derived from name+address) makes the two owners in the new test get *different* household segments, so a same-telephone create would be allowed (201) — but the test requires **409**. I confirmed this empirically. To satisfy the test *and* keep `identityKey` internally consistent with the returned `householdId`, I made `householdId` a **shared-household** identifier: derived only when the owner knowingly shares one (`sharesHousehold=true`), otherwise null. So two solo owners have an empty household segment → a telephone+email collision is a full-key match (409), while two household members with different telephones still differ by telephone and are both allowed — exactly the behaviour the spec describes. `householdSize` is now null-safe (a solo owner is a household of one).

3. **`OwnerMapper`** — added an `identityKey` derived mapping so the field is returned in the response.

4. **OpenAPI (`openapi.yml`)** — added the read-only `identityKey` property to the `Owner` schema (generates the DTO getter/setter).

5. **Advice/exception** — new `DuplicateIdentityException` and a handler in `ExceptionControllerAdvice` returning **409 Conflict** with `errors: ["identityKey"]`, mirroring the existing duplicate handlers. (The old duplicate exceptions/handlers remain but are now dormant.)

**Test results:** `AcceptanceTest.coreRejectsIdentityCollision` passes; full suite: `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — **BUILD SUCCESS**.

One note for a future checkpoint: `AcceptanceBase` mentions soft-delete excluding records from identity checks, but the current `Owner`/`deleteOwner` has no soft-delete concept, so `findAllOwners()` (used by the identity check) has nothing to exclude yet — not exercised by this change's tests.
